clue.text: Artist we hear wins election

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: to win an election in a constituency is, loosely, to gain a borough, said with the clipped British ending 'burra'

explanation.surface: A news report that some artist has triumphed at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'gains borough' (wins an election, a borough being a town that returns an MP) matches the painter Thomas Gainsborough.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was an eighteenth-century English portrait and landscape painter.

clue.text: Mythical maiden once suited the young

explanation.surface: A legendary girl who used to be just right for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a striped cotton fabric of that name, once used for children's sailor suits.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue brought to life for Pygmalion in Greek myth shares her name with an old cotton fabric for children's clothes.

clue.text: Pyrenean goat in Wizard of Oz

indicators.note: in tells us the goat is sitting inside the clue word Wizard

explanation.surface: A mountain goat turns up in the story of the Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the chamois as found in the Pyrenees mountains.

clue.text: Mirrors the heartless muse

parts.note: specula are mirrors, especially the reflectors in telescopes

indicators.note: heartless asks for the middle letter of the word the to be removed

explanation.surface: Mirrors described as the cold, unfeeling muse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a noun (the goddess) but is the verb, to ponder; THE loses its central H.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or wonder idly, which is to theorise without proof.

clue.text: Award holds nothing for music maker

indicators.note: holds means the award's letters wrap around the piece for nothing

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A prize contains nothing at all for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is something that makes music.

clue.text: Inflexible as a doubter perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of a doubter may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who doubts is as stubborn as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unwilling to change, unbending.

clue.text: Awkward week-ends in merry company

indicators.note: in places the week's ends inside the word for merry

parts.note: merry company is gay company; merry gives gay in its old sense of cheerful

indicators.note: ends of the word week asks for its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Feeling ungainly at weekends among cheerful friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Week-ends' looks like the weekend; it means the first and last letters W and K, which go inside GAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawky describes someone clumsy and ungainly, lacking grace.

clue.text: One rifle for example may bear such ornamentation

indicators.note: may bear hints the pieces carry their letters in a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
for example is abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A single gun might be decorated with delicate metalwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange I, RIFLE and EG; the whole clue also describes the fine wirework engraved on fancy guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental work of fine twisted metal threads.

clue.text: Put on platform but went by coach

explanation.surface: Mounted on a stage, yet travelled by bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is staged when put on; to stage once meant travelling by stagecoach.

clue.text: In the lead, holes out to land title

indicators.note: out signals the letters of lead and holes are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A golfer leading the field after holing out, about to win a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is tenure of property under a lease, a form of ownership right over land.

clue.text: Pastime once requiring silence

explanation.surface: A game that used to demand that everyone be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is a pastime; the old exclamation of that name was a call for hush.

clue.text: Report of service monotony

indicators.note: report of means we take the sound of the next word spoken

parts.note: the Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise sung at church services

explanation.surface: An account of a church service that was utterly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the dullness of boring sameness.

clue.text: Gourmet's starting with fish, followed by fish and fish again

indicators.note: starting with asks for the opening letter of the word Gourmet's

parts.note: the ray is a flat sea fish
ling is a long cod-like fish

explanation.surface: A food-lover's menu of one fish course after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The third 'fish' is the definition: a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Dog's blanket

explanation.surface: A rug belonging to the family pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The hound from the mountains of central Asia shares its name with a crocheted wool throw.

clue.text: Fresh and' wide awake? What a pest!

parts.note: fresh means green, as in new or unripe
fly is slang for alert and knowing

explanation.surface: Someone lively and alert proves to be a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are aphids, sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants.

clue.text: One of many in flight security

definitions.text: One of many in flight security

parts.words: One of many in flight security
parts.note: reads like airport safety, but the flight is a set of stairs whose carpet is held by many metal bars

explanation.surface: One of the many guards on an aeroplane journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar fixed across each step holds a staircase carpet in place.

clue.text: Neat filer creates an extra page

indicators.note: creates suggests building a new word from the letters of neat filer

explanation.surface: A tidy office clerk adds another sheet to the file.
explanation.definitionFit: An interleaf is a blank leaf bound between the printed pages of a book.

clue.text: Selections made by fishermen

explanation.surface: Choices that anglers make.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing actors for roles is casting; anglers also make casts of the line.

clue.text: Enable pi to be used as common denominator

indicators.note: to be used hints the letters of enable pi are to be put to work in another order

explanation.surface: A maths teacher using pi to find a lowest common denominator.
explanation.walkthrough: The maths phrase disguises the definition: a name (denominator) for the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebeian is one of the ordinary people, so the word labels the vulgar or lowborn.

clue.text: Rich heiress pictured in the lead?

definitions.text: Rich heiress pictured in the lead?

parts.words: Rich heiress pictured in the lead?
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice the wealthy heroine's portrait is hidden in the lead casket for her suitors to choose

explanation.surface: A wealthy young woman photographed leading the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the lead' suggests winning; it is the lead casket of Shakespeare's casket test.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Belmont heroine is a rich heiress whose image lay in the leaden casket.

clue.text: The way to Oxford from London?

definitions.text: The way to Oxford from London?

parts.words: The way to Oxford from London?
parts.note: looks like a route between two cities, but Oxford is a famous shopping road in London

explanation.surface: Asking directions from the capital to the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford Street is a major shopping road in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town is a way, and Oxford's is one of London's best known.

clue.text: Having means to get food in extremities

definitions.text: Having means to get food in extremities

parts.words: Having means to get food in extremities
parts.note: sounds like being able to eat only in desperate times, but describes a bird of prey's clawed feet

explanation.surface: Someone who can afford to eat only when things get desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk's claws are its means of seizing prey, so a clawed bird is so described.

clue.text: Make a fresh appearance

parts.note: reads like turning up again, but means giving something a new look

explanation.surface: Turning up again on the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore a building or room is to give it a new look.

clue.text: Plant given by doctor to the church

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor donates a plant to the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous plant of the pea family.

clue.text: The start of the composer's tour

indicators.note: start of asks for the opening letter of the word The

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: The opening night of a composer's concert tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour is to journey from place to place.

clue.text: Bill drops in to express an opinion

indicators.note: drops means the word in is let fall out of the bill

parts.note: an invoice is a bill for goods or services

explanation.surface: A man named Bill pops round to say what he thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill drops in' reads like a visit from a man called Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to state it aloud as one's view.

clue.text: Box for example like an old stager

explanation.surface: A container resembling a veteran actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is a hedge shrub; Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a kind of evergreen shrub or small timber plant, and Sir Herbert Tree was a famous stage actor.

clue.text: Opening, not out-some obstruction

parts.note: a batsman not out in cricket is still in
a let is a hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A gap that is still blocked to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow opening of the sea into the land.

clue.text: Warning — Old English is discordant as a language

indicators.note: is discordant hints the letters clash out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A warning that Old English sounds harsh compared with another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in Scandinavia's western kingdom is a language.

clue.text: Town man's overcoat with velvet collar

explanation.surface: A town gentleman wearing a smart coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield is a Derbyshire market town, and a tailored overcoat with a velvet collar shares its name.
